doc.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Big bands in Toronto
summary: Big bands are costly but several good ones exist in Toronto, including Boss Brass and his own.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Is there a big band scene still in Toronto or is it kind of an effort to mount every performance?

It’s tough to get the bands playing because of the practical aspect of it. It’s more difficult, it’s more expensive to hire seventeen pieces, but there are, in Toronto, several really good big bands. There’s Boss Brass of course which comes from there, and at the other end of the spectrum playing in this style is my own band, but in between there’s Dave McMurdo has a very good band, there’s quite a successful if somewhat commercial big band I attribute the Glenn Miller band, but it’s getting work and there’s The Spitfires, there’s Brigham Phyllis big band. I mean there’s half a dozen really good big bands up there. They’re not all working. But I mean I rehearse the big band. We get a handful of gigs every year, and the enthusiasm is there I think.
